blocks.text: PONTIANAK, Indonesia — Every few years, residents of Indonesia’s West Kalimantan province contend with devastating wildfires that emit a noxious haze causing illnesses, shuttering schools and stifling economic activity. Now, they’ve had enough. Lawyers have filed a class action case claiming “negligence, omission and failure” on the part of the government that has resulted in “a massive public health crisis” in the province on Borneo island. READ: Indonesia’s haze returns a decade after its worst fires. Why?
